title: DVC Mallorca source lifecycle and reproduction spike
hypothesis: DVC can manage a real bounded Mallorca terrain source through content-addressed storage, deletion, rehydration, preparation, reuse and deterministic reproduction without changing YACS production paths.
technical: DVC 3.67.1 imported a 99,090-byte official CNIG/IDEE Mallorca MDT05 GeoTIFF and stored it in an isolated local remote.
After deleting the raw working file and nested local DVC cache, dvc pull restored the source with the same SHA-256.
DVC restored prepared outputs from the proof remote and a forced dvc repro regenerated the heightfield and report byte-identically.
The final DVC status reported that data and pipelines were up to date; two deterministic preparation tests passed.
visual: No visual acceptance was required: this is a storage and reproducibility proof, not an Unreal terrain-quality proof.
keep: DVC as the candidate raw/prepared storage and pipeline engine for the next Issue #339 architecture step.
A thin YACS layer for policy, provenance, profiles, diagnostics and SHA-256 verification.
The isolated uv-locked experiment and fail-closed Windows lifecycle runner.
reject: Building a custom content-addressed storage engine before DVC is evaluated against a production remote and another provider.
Treating the experimental heightfield, local proof remote or CNIG sample as production authority.
Claiming DVC's internal filesystem object key is SHA-256; this proof observed MD5 identities in DVC descriptors/cache.
learnings: DVC can reuse both raw and derived objects after the working tree and local cache are removed.
Windows hardlink cache objects are read-only and require bounded attribute handling in destructive lifecycle tests.
Project-level SHA-256 provenance can coexist with DVC's internal object identity, but must remain an explicit YACS verification contract.
next: Choose and prove a durable shared DVC remote before integrating DVC behind the future yacs assets/bootstrap UX.
Integrate one existing provider only after the #339 storage contract and profile semantics are agreed.
Keep all production code, manifests, downloaders and Unreal Content unchanged until that follow-up scope is approved.
